reason: While the text does contain named characters—specifically Moses (מֹשֶׁה), Aaron (אַהֲרֹן), and Pharaoh (פַּרְעֹה)—none of them qualify as 'regular people.' Moses and Aaron are portrayed as divinely chosen prophets and leaders with supernatural authority and divine commission. Pharaoh is a ruler with supreme authority over Egypt. All named characters in this passage occupy extraordinary positions with special status. The text mentions other people (Israelites, Egyptians, Pharaoh's servants) but only in collective, unnamed groups. There are no named characters depicted as ordinary or regular people.
